note.text: Editing requires a diagnosis before a correction. Identify the intended meaning and the relevant pattern: agreement, reference, word form or clause boundary. The nearest noun does not necessarily control a verb. A comma alone cannot join independent clauses in the taught formal model. Different acceptable English varieties may use different patterns, so distinguish the specified edited model from a claim that every local use lacks meaning.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to identify a specific error and make a meaning-preserving repair. Builds on: word roles, clause structure and reference. Leads to: comparison and descriptive drafting.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original editing examples: The list of items is ready agrees with list, not items. Bih spoke to Ngozi; the pronoun she may need clarification if either could be meant. We waited because the room was locked expresses a reason. We waited, the room was locked needs a suitable boundary or an explicit connector in this edited model.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Read for meaning, mark the exact faulty relationship and repair only what is needed. Check the whole result for a new error. If more than one repair is possible, state what meaning your chosen connector creates.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve the intended meaning and form.
example: The nearest plural noun always requires a plural verb. Correction: The head of the subject, not every nearby noun, controls this agreement.
Every pronoun has exactly one possible referent in every context. Correction: Context or repetition may be needed to clarify reference.
Every comma can replace a full stop between independent clauses. Correction: Use a suitable connector, semicolon or full stop for this relationship.
Any grammatical connector preserves exactly the same relation. Correction: Different connectors can change time, condition, reason or contrast.

pick.q: Choose the edited agreement: The list of requests ___ ready.
e: Requests is inside an of phrase; list is the subject head.
Be alone is not the present finite form needed.
That sequence does not form the intended predicate.
pick.y: The singular head list controls is.

pick.q: Two independent clauses are intended with no causal claim: Bih checked the note, Tabe waited. Which minimal formal repair preserves that?
pick.r: Bih checked the note; Tabe waited.
w: Bih checked the note Tabe waited.
Bih checked the note, because Tabe always lied.
e: Removing punctuation leaves a fused sentence.
That leaves only a dependent clause and drops the other event.
The invented cause and lying claim change the message.
pick.y: A semicolon can join related independent clauses without adding a cause.

pick.q: Bih told Ngozi that she would lead. The writer means Ngozi. Which repair makes that reference explicit?
pick.r: Bih told Ngozi that Ngozi would lead.
w: Bih told Ngozi that Bih would lead.
e: That selects the other person.
That removes the stated plan.
That contradicts the speech event.
pick.y: Repeating the intended name removes this ambiguity.
